labels.label: def:cauchy_embedding_cauchy_extension
labels.notes: This is an instance, not a certificate. It is unmarked and partial, which is correct. cauchyExtension proves everything with no assumed hypothesis. For every Cauchy time function T of E0 strictly increasing along <= (one exists: exists_cauchyTimeFunction = E0.geroch_sing_i_imp_ii) and every a, sublevel a = {T < a} is E0Covered (e0Covered_opens). Its natural causality exists and is unique (existsUnique_isE0Natural). For each natural C: AbsolutelyMinimal (hC.2.2); IsoChartsCoverDEC25 (SFALocal.isoChartsCoverDEC25_of_e0); the relations at the top are E0's (relations_top_iff composed with le/lt_iff_le/lt_top_of_isPast); C is GloballyHyperbolic (isCausal_opens, and the diamonds are E0's and lie inside {T < a}); every i^-1(T^-1 b) with b < a is a Cauchy surface; and IsCauchyEmbedding C E0.causality Subtype.val holds, which is the real DEC-17 structure: both sides GH, IsEMorphism, injective, and i^-1(T^-1(a-1)) is carried onto a Cauchy surface of E0. The inclusion is not Surjective, because the tau-orbit of the axis meets T^-1(a). The DEC-25 reading is the one the M-level rows use. #synth gives opensSingularGXStructure (sublevel _ 1) as the instance on the subtype, and T2Space and SecondCountableTopology are the subtype instances, so they are synthesised, not assumed. Connectedness is also proved (connectedSpace_sublevel, singularFlatSpacetime_sublevel), so M is a singular flat spacetime in the sense of def:singular_spacetime as well. The hypotheses hT, hTs and hC are inhabited (nonvacuous_e0 at a = 1, b = 0).

labels.label: lem:image_diamant
labels.notes: image_diamant_witness takes its conclusion from SingularRowsDiamond.image_diamant. The hypotheses hmin, hC, hminN, hCN, hi and hS all come from cauchyExtension and SFALocal.nonvacuous_e0, and hp is proved. The point is the axis point with T = (a+b)/2: it lies in J+_M(Sigma) minus Sigma, and the statement only says b < T p. The first conjunct, not J+(T^-1 b) contained in range i, shows that the inclusion is no longer the identity's trivial one. The docstring describes exactly what the theorem states. One wording point (finding 1): the module docstring says every row is instantiated 'at points of the frontier T^-1(a)', but this row's point is interior, as the lemma requires. Its conclusion also follows directly from the past-set property of {T < a}. Unmarked and partial, which is correct.

labels.label: lem:passe_pgcd
labels.notes: Both branches are taken from SingularRowsDiamond.passe_pgcd_printed, and its hypothesis is met at frontier points that lie outside range i. This closes the gap of T-ett-diamant-rows AUDIT-1, where frontier(range id) was empty. passe_pgcd_btz_witness uses p1 = tauFlow ta (0,0), on the axis with T p1 = a. It proves p1 in frontier(range i), via the limit along the axis from below and the fact that range i is open. It proves p1 not in range i, p1 in J+(T^-1 b), the K- inclusion, the BTZ explicit form (hrow.2.2), and that (J+(T^-1 b) cap J-(p1)) minus {p1} is non-empty: it contains the axis point with T = b. passe_pgcd_regular_witness uses q1 = tauFlow ta (0,1): off the axis by tauFlow_mem_axis, in the frontier, outside range i, in J+. It proves the K- inclusion, the regular explicit form (hrow.2.1), and that I-(q1) cap J+(T^-1 b) is non-empty, via q1 in Z- and the cover argument. nonvacuous_e0 assembles both at a = 1, b = 0. The docstrings describe exactly what each theorem exercises. As for image_diamant, the conclusions also follow directly from {T < a} being a past set (finding 1). Unmarked and partial, which is correct.

labels.label: lem:Cauchy_plongement_toutes
labels.notes: plongement_witness takes its conclusion from SingularRowsCauchy.cauchy_plongement_toutes_manifolds, applied to the inclusion, which is not onto. Every hypothesis is discharged: hmin, hcov and hG come from cauchyExtension, hminN and hCN from SFALocal.nonvacuous_e0, then E0.globallyHyperbolic, hi.isEMorphism and hi.injective. It gives (i) <=> (ii), (ii) itself through hi.exists_cauchy, and for every c < a that i^-1(T^-1 c) is Cauchy in M and its image is Cauchy in E0. The docstring describes this exactly. Unmarked and partial, which is correct.

findings.what: The docstring says the rows are instantiated 'at points of the frontier T^-1(a), where their conclusions are no longer trivial'. This overstates in two ways. First, only passe_pgcd's points lie on the frontier: image_diamant's point is interior (T p = (a+b)/2, in M, as the lemma requires), and plongement_witness has no point. Second, i(M) = {T < a} is a past set of E0 and T is strictly increasing along <=, so every witnessed conclusion also follows in a line from isPast_sublevel and the relations clause of cauchyExtension. For T p <= a, J-(p) minus {p} lies in {T < a}, which gives both branches of passe_pgcd and the K- inclusion, and with the equal relations it also gives image_diamant's equality. The witnesses do achieve what the target asked: the rows' hypotheses are met with range i not equal to N and p in the frontier of i(M). But they do not exercise anything the past-set property does not already give.
